diagrams.title: From Federal Dollar to Sealed Complaint
diagrams.subtitle: Five moves practitioners use to preserve original-source status and relator share
diagrams.caption: Relators who win pair a material defect with insider documents, serve the written disclosure before filing, and plead the full 10-year window under a seal that runs 60 days on paper and about 2.5 years in practice.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Step order follows the operator gates and pro-tips quoted by the cited practitioners; seal length, the 11-month intervention average, the 10-year window, and the 29 states plus DC figure are reported practitioner claims, not independently verified.
diagrams.note: Sources: Justia (Hamilton and Newman, HocnawRgrAA), Beverly Hills Bar Association (Mark Kleiman, yN7NRjwYKFs), Phillips & Cohen LLP (5-ptDaAQkvI), Shipman Wright Law (7-9Z8vNWVFc), Brown, LLC (3ugChIElhkM).

stages.label: Materiality check
stages.detail: Confirm the defect is one the payer would refuse to pay for, like out-of-spec military parts rather than wrong-color parts (Justia, Hamilton and Newman).

stages.label: Photograph the documents
stages.detail: Take pictures of documents instead of walking out with them, and audit your own involvement first because dirty hands cut the award (Kleiman; Brown, LLC).

stages.label: Serve written disclosure
stages.detail: Serve the written disclosure statement with all material evidence before filing the complaint (Phillips & Cohen LLP).

stages.label: File the sealed complaint
stages.detail: Plead the full 10-year limitations window plus parallel state counts; 29 states plus DC have FCAs (Justia; Beverly Hills Bar Association).

stages.label: Hold the seal in silence
stages.detail: No media contact while DOJ averages about 11 months to decide intervention; public information disqualifies a relator (Phillips & Cohen; Shipman Wright Law).

diagrams.title: Referral Arrangements Priced in Settlements and Per-Claim Penalties
diagrams.subtitle: Dollar figures quoted for Stark and Anti-Kickback exposure, largest to smallest
diagrams.caption: Wheeling Hospital's net-revenue physician pay settled for $50M with $10M to a former-executive relator; free call coverage at Catholic Medical Center cost $3.8M; per-claim penalties stack on every referral-tainted claim.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Stages are ordered by quoted dollar size rather than a single conversion path; per-claim figures are practitioner-quoted and adjust for inflation over time.
diagrams.note: Sources: KLGatesLaw (MMcEwUD0PNo), Holland & Hart LLP (wODno0XW8l4), OIGatHHS (Meredith Williams, a4KhqqeAaUg).

stages.label: Wheeling Hospital settlement
stages.conversion: Motion to dismiss denied before settlement
stages.detail: Physicians paid a percentage of net revenue tracked in physician impact reports (KLGatesLaw).

stages.label: Wheeling relator share
stages.detail: Referral spreadsheets tied to pay were the gap; firewall them or stop keeping them (KLGatesLaw).

stages.label: Catholic Medical Center settlement
stages.conversion: Bona fide employee safe harbor did not apply
stages.detail: Free call coverage that other cardiologists were paid $10,000 per weekend to provide (KLGatesLaw).

stages.label: Stark penalty per claim
stages.conversion: Adjusted for inflation; can add up really quickly
stages.detail: Exclusion, FCA treble damages, and qui tam suits layer on top (Holland & Hart LLP).

stages.label: FCA kickback penalty per claim
stages.detail: Up to three times the program's loss plus $11,000 per claim (OIGatHHS, Meredith Williams).

diagrams.title: USIS Dumping Case Recovery Walk
diagrams.subtitle: How an intervened settlement splits, and what declining severance preserved
diagrams.caption: Blake Percival took 20 percent of an about $30M intervened settlement, about $6M, after turning down $42,000 in severance that carried a fine-print waiver of whistleblower rights.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Result bars are straight subtraction of the quoted figures; counsel contingency fees and taxes were not quantified by the practitioners and are excluded.

diagrams.title: Seal and Decision Clocks Relators Should Expect
diagrams.subtitle: Reported ranges for seal renewals, total seal time, and case resolution
diagrams.caption: Seals renew 6 months at a time, total periods of 8 months, 14 months, or a couple of years are common, and many cases finish two or three years after filing.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Years converted to months (a couple of years shown as 24); where no point estimate was quoted, typical marks the lower bound of the stated range.
diagrams.note: Sources: Stephen Teller - Teller Law (SiATzxJHy2Y), Phillips & Cohen LLP (5-ptDaAQkvI), Tycko & Zavareei LLP (Jon Tycko, A2nRu5da_9k).

diagrams.title: Medicare and Medicaid Billing Fraud Reporting Gates
diagrams.subtitle: Four checks before an insider files a False Claims Act case
diagrams.caption: Systemic provider fraud proven with knowing conduct pays 15 to 30 percent; intervened cases average about $13M against about $3M declined, so speed and clean evidence matter.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order is a sequencing of the operator gates quoted by the cited practitioners; settlement averages are Brown's generalized statistics, not case guarantees.
diagrams.note: Sources: Brown, LLC (Jason T. Brown, faQOCnnY-QI, nDO81fwnTqg, 7two8gR6AAY), Stephen Teller - Teller Law (0w534uBbqVQ), Baker Donelson (Tom Barnard, -Vss5I_7dHM).

nodes.question: Is the target systemic billing fraud by a provider rather than a neighbor misusing benefits?
nodes.fail_action: Report directly to the government; individual benefit cases are not the qui tam lane (Brown, LLC).

nodes.question: Can you show knowing conduct, including reckless disregard or deliberate ignorance, with emails or firsthand facts?
nodes.fail_action: A nurse disagreeing with medical necessity is a tough case to make; keep documenting (Teller).

nodes.question: Is every billing statement, email, or medical record one you are lawfully entitled to access?
nodes.fail_action: Stop gathering and call whistleblower counsel first to avoid termination or criminal exposure (Brown, LLC).

nodes.question: Are you clear of signing, profiting, or handing over a Medicare number?
nodes.pass_next: File fast with counsel; only the first to file has rights (Brown, LLC; Barnard).
nodes.fail_action: Assume personal exposure and raise it with counsel before any report (Brown, LLC).

diagrams.title: Who Touches a Form 211 Claim
diagrams.subtitle: The Whistleblower Office bottleneck and the lanes around it
diagrams.caption: About 1,000 claims a month reach 32 reviewers, so only documented, insider-sourced, collectible claims above the $2,000,000 floor get traction, and nothing pays until appeals are exhausted.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Intake load, reviewer count, and thresholds are practitioner-reported; Brown adds that the IRS rarely moves below a likely $10 million collection.
diagrams.note: Sources: Where IRS Problems Get Solved (Eric Green, ruRW_hNSDYk), The Anti-Fraud Coalition (Emily Stibil, fQss6bE5tKc), Brown, LLC (tQIkb01vCTw), Former IRS Agent Representation (41ejxu80Qtg, QxVllUQ7IRk), Logan Allec (i4GnKgGXiMw).

center.focus: About 1,000 claims per month, roughly 30 to 35 new files per reviewer each month

spokes.kpi: More than $2,000,000 in dispute; over $200,000 gross income for individual targets
Narrative memo with enabling-party, witness, and document appendices handed over on day one
Collection potential proven before filing; 15 to 30 percent paid only on proceeds collected
Conviction rates rather than collections; wants a large, near-perfect case

diagrams.title: What Repayment Costs at Each Exit
diagrams.subtitle: Multiples of single damages quoted for disclosure, settlement, and judgment
diagrams.total_range: 1.25x to 3x single damages, before per-claim penalties
diagrams.caption: The civil self-disclosure pilot prices repayment at 1.25 to 1.6x against typical FCA settlements at about 2x, while treble damages plus per-claim penalties await at judgment.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Multipliers are practitioner-quoted bands; per-claim penalties sit on top of the trebled figure and are not folded into the multiples.
diagrams.note: Sources: Seyfarth Shaw LLP (Tori Young, QLVKZRh_ArE), ClearanceJobs (Julie Bracker, j_QEFJG-ON4), Justia (Hamilton and Newman, HocnawRgrAA).

buckets.label: Civil self-disclosure pilot
buckets.notes: No factual admissions, CIA, CMPs, or revocations; deadline April 22, 2027 (Tori Young).

buckets.label: Typical FCA settlement
buckets.notes: About 2x, the benchmark Tori Young contrasted with the pilot.

buckets.label: Government net after one-third relator cut
buckets.notes: Even at one-third, the government still nets double damages (Bracker).

buckets.label: Treble damages at judgment
buckets.notes: Plus $13,000 to $27,000 per claim as quoted by Hamilton and Newman.

diagrams.title: Detection Starts With Records You Already Hold
diagrams.subtitle: A four-week build pairing bank-feed testing with a hotline
diagrams.caption: Hotline-only shops are already behind; Workman Forensics pairs monthly bank-feed tests with tips, and GRF reports hotline usage up 16% over ten years.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The four-week sequencing is an ordering of the cited practitioners' gates; the practitioners did not prescribe a weekly schedule.
diagrams.note: Sources: Workman Forensics (4CnIVLSoe2o), GRF CPAs & Advisors (bPsS_B4v7Dw), Koegle Law Group (nM5JZ33rgDk), The Brad Weisman Show (Sherry Peel Jackson, _ehHXyRo6fI).

weeks.title: Export and account check
weeks.deliverable: Payroll exports to Excel and owners named on every business bank account
weeks.gate: If the payroll provider cannot export, change providers (Workman Forensics).

weeks.title: Bank-feed testing
weeks.deliverable: Monthly or quarterly tests and macros running on bank feeds
weeks.gate: No hotline-only detection; tips arrive late and the reporter may have been in the scam (Workman Forensics).

weeks.title: Hotline intake
weeks.deliverable: Good-faith certification checkbox on every intake report, beyond mail-and-fax intake
weeks.gate: Written policy in place before ticking yes on the 990 whistleblower disclosure (GRF CPAs & Advisors).

weeks.title: Investigation and expense scrub
weeks.deliverable: Outside investigator assigned; round-number expenses stripped and receipts kept
weeks.gate: In-house HR bias screened out (Koegle Law Group); round numbers are the top audit red flag (Jackson).
